sources.name: Washington Legislative Web Services

access.rateLimit: No numeric quota, pagination contract, row cap, response-size bound, concurrency limit, timeout, retry policy, or backoff rule is published. A future adapter must use bounded, low-concurrency, build-time requests and fail closed on repository-owned request, item, byte, and time budgets.

coverage.cadence: LWS describes its source data as real-time; any approved Policy Sentinel retrieval would remain weekly and build-time only.
coverage.limitations: No service-wide historical start or complete mutation feed is documented. LegislativeDocumentService explicitly describes information back to 1991-92, and the separate Detailed Legislative Reports UI describes bill information back to 1991, but required operation ranges remain unverified. Arrays are unbounded, no pagination is published, response fields include personal/contact and unrelated free text, and no official bill-subject operation exists.

access.rateLimit: No numeric request limit, quota, response-size bound, retry rule, SLA, checksum, page-update cadence, or change-notification contract was published. coverage.cadence: GOIA publishes no update cadence for the Accord page; Policy Sentinel would verify the one selected page weekly and build-time only.
coverage.limitations: This is one selected official HTML transcription, not a signed facsimile or complete accord registry. It identifies collective signatory parties and an execution date but no individual Nation signatories, unique accord number, source update time, complete amendment or supersession history, or reuse license. The current record model cannot preserve parties, an executed date, and accord status without forcing them into unrelated fields, so adapter implementation is blocked.
